For x=η the shear pullback is the ordinary first-coordinate centroid cap in T. Zero shift gives 2ΓV and the accepted paired bound matches it, so the x=η competitor justifies the full |x|≤η minimization domain before the explicit formula is used.

For 0<a≤1/6, the accepted fixed-normal proof keeps the same oriented height order and finds any positive minimum either saturated or properly straddling. Proper straddling is strictly concave, and the support and branch knots are covered by the accepted derivative analysis. Thus the strict comparison of the exact zero-shift cost with V makes zero optimal. At a=0 and m=1/3 both shifted proper caps give a convex quadratic for 0≤σ≤1/3, since the upper threshold is at most 2/3. For larger shifts the lower cap is full and the cost is at least V.

The positive vertical direction is the unperturbed coordinate cap at zero shift. In the negative vertical direction, for uniform X on T the variable 1−X_2 has density 2s on [0,1] and the centered projection is (1−X_2)−2/3. The accepted planar equality example therefore matches at shift 1/3, with the general paired bound giving the reverse inequality.

The two width exponents add to one, and M_η has determinant one, so E_t has area tV and lies in int T for small t. The accepted exact-hull theorem applies with a=V at the displayed seven sites, including its exact six-fiber formula, owned-fiber correction, compact maximizing localization, and other-site bounds.

Canonical trial caps have cost ΓV+O(t) because a saturated opposite shift has normalized pair cost V. Joint cap continuity and exact oriented centroid equality exclude all limiting normals outside the three rays. At an actual near-minimizing ambient cap the pair contribution is bounded below by the minimized pair at its normal.

For u=(1,δ), only e_1 is strictly included near (g,(1,0)). Its two edge height differences are 1 and 1−δ, and its included margin is (2−δ)/3−t(v_{t,1}+δv_{t,2}). This gives the exact square formula and own excess Vδ²/[9(1−δ)]. The mark change is −κtv_1+o(t), so every competing such δ is O(√t).

For bounded x_t=δ/√t, the E_t projection scale t^(3/4) gives direction (1,x_t) on B and mark threshold t^(1/4)(v_{t,1}+δv_{t,2}). Bounded projection support gives a single compact shift domain, and every convergent shift sequence has area-null limiting boundaries. This proves uniform convergence of the two cap costs on the shift domain and hence convergence of their minima.

The centroid paired inequality for B and the x=η trial exclude |x|>η. On the remaining interval the exact fixed-normal formula gives H. Its derivative and strict positive second derivative follow by rewriting (x−η)^2/(1−x+η) as (1−x+η)−2+(1−x+η)^−1. Direct rational evaluation of the stated cubic at the two bracket endpoints gives −2681205623/10^13 and 3419174933/(125·10^10), with opposite signs. The two squares cannot simultaneously vanish.

At the other two rays the scale t^(1/4) gives limiting directions +Y and −Y, with negligible mark threshold O(t^(3/4)). Their minimized pair constants are equal, although the −Y optimum uses nonzero shift. The own cap is smooth in these ray neighborhoods, and its change at the canonical normal is −κt l_i(v)+o(t); the own centroid excess for competing normals remains nonnegative.

The lower subsequence bounds and the three admissible trials give the exact limiting score. At v_* the three scores coincide, so any near-optimal l_1 sequence has every bounded scaled normal cluster point minimizing H, giving the asserted convergence.

The linear barycentric map is a bijection onto the zero-sum score-coordinate plane, so equalization is the unique maximizer and gives v_*=(Δ,−Δ/2). The accepted O(t) localization permits passage along every maximizing selection. The positive mean paired score strictly separates the winning base from all other exact bounds. Dividing by 2+(3/2)t gives 7/18+Δ/6; at v=0 the coefficient is 17/18.
